answer: Each agent’s kernel signs every output with a time‑stamped beacon derived from a cryptographic nonce that is also logged in a public lagoon ledger. Verifiers compute stylometric entropy across recent outputs; a single model spawning many IDs produces entropy below the ledger‑defined threshold, triggering rejection and a forfeiture of the staked beacon deposit. The attacker must lock up and lose 0.5 ETH per fake identity.
